findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.comment: Observed three bags of deli ham in the walk in cooler that were date marked 2/5-2/11. Ham was discarded during the inspection as these are past the 7 day date marking for TCS foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41?F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Observed chicken cooling since 1 pm in a bag in the reach in cooler that was probed at an internal temperature of 90-107F. A pan of rice in the walk in cooler was cooling since the same time and probed at 108F. Time cooling began was not indicated on the items and cooling logs are not kept. Cooling must be done rapidly rather than placed in a cooler and forgotten. Chicken was moved to an ice bath and one portion of rice was saved to continued to be cooled. Use rapid cooling methods to cool from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and then to 41F or below within an additional 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Single-service articles are not protected from contamination. Single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food and lip contact surfaces are protected from contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment: 1) Observed the sprayer nozzle in the dish room to rest on the table and below the flood rim. 2) Observed the drain pipe from the dish machine to extend down into the floor drain. Provide proper air gap/backflow prevention for the sprayer and the dish machine.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.13  (P) An air gap is not properly provided. The water supply inlet is below the flood rim of the fixture/equipment. Provide an air gap at least twice the diameter of the water supply inlet or at least 1 inch. Reference 5-202.13.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed deli meat in the walk in cooler dated 7/2-7/9 and tuna salad in the reach in cooler dated 7/4-7/11. These are past the 7 days allowed for ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods. It also looks as though all of the date marking ranges are exceeding 7 days as the day that you open or prepare the food counts as a full Day 1. Foods prepared on Monday are only good through Sunday and then must be discarded. These items were discarded during the inspection.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text: 750.830 - Dish machine tested at 0ppm chlorine. Machine tested at 50ppm around 7am according to chart kept by dish room staff. findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 - Water at handsinks had an obvious temperature difference between hot and cold, but the hot water was sometimes warm. Manager wasn't sure if water usage in other parts of the building might be affecting the temperature. Laundry was being done across the hall. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Have a licensed plumber check on the issue and make any repairs that may be required.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Ceramic coving at the wall across from 2 part sink had a gap in it along the top & an area with a small hole - Repair the wall & seal the gap. B) Coving was missing at the corner of the wall by the door in the walkin cooler & the bottom section of the wall covering was staring to pull up - Repair/properly seal the wall & along the floor of the cooler. C) Floor drain at the 3 part sink did not have a cover down inside - Provide a drain cover. D) Floors in the walkin freezer & cooler were observed to be soiled with food/general debris under shelves/along walls. Clean the floors in the walkin units.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 - A) Holes were observed in the wall of the dish room below the clean dish counter (area by dish machine floor drain). B) Exhaust fan above the dish machine was loose. A gap was present between the fan & the ceiling. Walls, ceilings, & attached fixtures must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents. Repair the walls & ceiling/exhaust fan in the dish area. **Check throughout the kitchen and seal any holes observed.**

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 - Hole was observed in the dish area in the corner by the handsink at the top of the coving. The hole was caulked during the inspection. **Maintain floor to wall joints.**

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 - Holes were observed in the walls in the dish area. The holes were caulked during the inspection. All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents. **Re-caulk the areas in question as needed.**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - Can opener blade had food debris on it and was not currently in use. Clean and sanitize all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of food, mold, and other debris. The can opener was taken to the dish area/ran through the dish machine during the inspection.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text: 750.1160 - Fruit flies were observed around the snack station by the 2 compartment sink (~4-5) and in the dish area (+12). Effective measures to minimize the presence of pests shall be utilized. A service call has been made to Ecolab for service. Thoroughly clean the dish area and seal any cracks, gaps, or crevices in floors and walls (see #36 & #37 for details). Fly strips can be used if appropriately placed away from food, prep areas, and clean equipment (i.e. in corner by the office door and in dish area in corner above handsink or on the underside of dish counter). Provide Ecolab invoice for service at follow up inspection.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Hole was observed in the dish area in the corner by the handsink at the top of the coving. B) The dish machine floor drain and drain cover were observed to be soiled. Fill in the hole above the coving. Clean the floor drain and the cover in the dish room. Thoroughly clean the floor throughout the entire dish room and minimize standing water. **Clean all floors throughout under equipment, under shelves, and along walls/in corners daily/as needed.**

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 & 1220 - A) Holes were observed in the walls in the dish area. B) Walls under dish machine/underside of dish counter were soiled (small amount of buildup and food debris). All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents. Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Fill in the holes and any other cracks or crevices that may be present. Clean the walls and the underside of the dish counter.
